newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel firms $1 but bearish Russian exports loom.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel firms $1 but bearish Russian exports loom.

text.p: European heavy fuel oil firmed $1 a tonne on Wednesday ahead of the Ascension day public holiday across much of Europe on Thursday.
Europe remained the cheapest region for heavy fuel and dealers expect exports to both to Asia and the United States.
"You should see a lot of fuel moving out of the region," said a Swiss-based trader.
Rotterdam barges traded up to $83 fob on pre-holiday bunker demand estimated at around 20,000 tonnes.
Cargoes were also said to be bouyant with levels pegged around $81 or even a shade higher delivered to Rotterdam.

But a bearish cloud has begun to form over the summer market. Although river ice has delayed barge deliveries to St Peterburgs by a few days river borne exports are expected to be sharply higher this summer.
A Western trader based at the port told Reuters he expected up to 4.5 million tonnes to be exported from St Petersburg between May and November.
In total summer exports are expected to average close to 1.3 million tonnes a month from St Petersburg, Tallin, Ventspils, Klaepeda, Arkhangelsk and Kandalaksha, said other traders.
